summary: Get approved for accommodations such as extra exam time, then share them with your instructors each semester.
whoFor: Enrolled CMU students with a sensory, physical, emotional or cognitive disability. You can apply at any time.
steps: Log in with your Andrew ID and complete the online application.
Wait for ODR to confirm they received your form.
Submit documentation following ODR's documentation guidelines.
Book a meeting with ODR to talk about your needs.
If approved, send your Summary of Accommodations Memo to your instructors through the portal at the start of each semester.

locations.notes: Mon to Fri, 8:30 am to 5 pm, by appointment only

prepare: Current documentation from a licensed provider that includes your diagnosis, how it affects you, and recommended accommodations (CaPS can help you put this together)
expect: After you apply, you meet with ODR to discuss accommodations. If you want to change approved accommodations later, email ODR; they reply within 5 business days.

summary: A first conversation with a CaPS therapist to figure out what support fits you, from short-term therapy to groups or a referral.
whoFor: Undergraduate and graduate students enrolled at the Pittsburgh campus.
limits: Short-term therapy; most students use 6 to 8 sessions. No limit on consultations or crisis support.
steps: Call CaPS at 412-268-2922 and ask to schedule a consultation.
Set a reminder. CaPS also emails a reminder the business day before.

locations.building: Highmark Center for Health, Wellness & Athletics

prepare: A few minutes to make the call
A rough idea of what you want help with (it's fine if you're not sure)
script: Hi, my name is ___ and I'd like to schedule a consultation.
expect: You'll be seen within 5 business days. Sessions are 45 to 50 minutes. The first meeting focuses on getting to know your needs and deciding next steps together. If it's urgent, you can walk in or call to be screened for a same-day appointment.
internalNotes: Open question: which of the two offices hosts consultations?

summary: A weekly support group where neurodivergent students share experiences and support each other, led by a CaPS therapist.
steps: Email the facilitator or call CaPS to schedule a pre-group consultation.
Attend the pre-group consultation to talk through whether the group fits your needs.
prepare: A pre-group consultation before your first session
script: Hi, my name is ___ and I'd like to schedule a pre-group consultation for the Neurodistinct support group.
expect: Groups are confidential: members agree not to share what's said outside the group.
internalNotes: Open questions: confirm with CaPS that this is the group the outline called Neurospicy, and which room it meets in.

summary: A quiet room to rest, breathe and recharge, with comfy seating, yoga mats and calm activities like coloring and puzzles.

space.hours: Open 24 hours during fall and spring semesters
space.seating: Anti-gravity chairs, meditation cushions, yoga mats
space.rules: No homework or meetings; the room is for resting.

internalNotes: Open question: confirm the right contact (outline listed Harsh Agarwal). Official page says both first and ground floor; guestsAllowed not stated, so left out.

summary: Shared work sessions with other students to help each other stay on task.
steps: Details to be confirmed with the Student Academic Success Center.
